# Radio group: `jl-radio-group`

One choice among a few, all in view, as radios or as cards.

- Class `JlRadioGroup`, a molecule: `import { JlRadioGroup } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/radio-group

One choice among a few that should all stay in view: a plan, a size, a frequency. For a long list,
prefer a select.

It behaves as native radios: Tab reaches the chosen option (or the first one), the arrow keys move the choice and
skip disabled options, Space chooses the focused option. The label names the group for screen readers; with legend
it is also shown over the options. variant="cards" draws each option as a bordered card, for choices that deserve a
line of explanation.

## Use

```ts
import { JlRadioGroup } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlRadioGroup
  label="Plan"
  legend
  options={[{"description":"One project, community support.","label":"Hobby","value":"hobby"},{"description":"Unlimited projects, email support.","label":"Pro","value":"pro"},{"description":"SSO, audit logs and a contract.","label":"Enterprise","value":"enterprise"}]}
  value="pro"
/>
```

```html
<jl-radio-group
  label="Plan"
  legend
  options='[{"description":"One project, community support.","label":"Hobby","value":"hobby"},{"description":"Unlimited projects, email support.","label":"Pro","value":"pro"},{"description":"SSO, audit logs and a contract.","label":"Enterprise","value":"enterprise"}]'
  value="pro"
></jl-radio-group>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `options` (attribute `options`): `RadioOption<Value>[]`, default `[]`. The choices: value, label, and an optional description and disabled.
- `value` (attribute `value`): `Value | ''`, default `''`. The chosen value; empty while nothing is chosen.
- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. The group's name for screen readers.
- `legend` (attribute `legend`): `boolean`, default `false`. Shows the label over the options.
- `orientation` (attribute `orientation`): `'vertical' | 'horizontal'`, default `'vertical'`. Options in a column or in a row.
- `variant` (attribute `variant`): `'plain' | 'cards'`, default `'plain'`. A dot beside each label, or a bordered card per option.
- `name` (attribute `name`): `string`, default `''`. The field's name in the form's data.
- `required` (attribute `required`): `boolean`, default `false`. The form cannot be submitted until an option is chosen.
- `disabled` (attribute `disabled`): `boolean`, default `false`. No option can be chosen or focused.

## Events

In JSX, the `on…` prop, its handler given the detail; in code, `events.register(name, (detail) => …)`. They do not bubble.

- `change` (`onChange` in JSX), detail `Value`: Someone chose an option.

## Methods

- `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void`: Focuses the chosen option, or the first one that can be chosen.
- `checkValidity(): boolean`: Whether a required group has a choice.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The radiogroup element around the options.
- `--dot` (custom property): The size of the dots (18px).

## Typing

Typed by its values, JlRadioGroup<'hobby' | 'pro' | 'team'> takes options of those values only, and gives change and value as one of them: the editor completes them and refuses another. In JSX, the type can also be read from the options.

```ts
import type { JlRadioGroup } from '@syware/jlib';

type Plan = 'hobby' | 'pro' | 'team';

const plan = document.querySelector<JlRadioGroup<Plan>>('jl-radio-group.plan');
plan?.options.set([
  { label: 'Hobby', value: 'hobby' },
  { label: 'Pro', value: 'pro' },
  { label: 'Team', value: 'team' },
]);
// @ts-expect-error: 'free' is not a plan
plan?.value.set('free');
plan?.events.register('change', (value) => choosePlan(value)); // value: Plan
```

```tsx
import { Jadis } from '@jadis/core';
import { JlRadioGroup } from '@syware/jlib';

import type { RadioOption } from '@syware/jlib';

type Plan = 'hobby' | 'pro' | 'team';

const PLANS: RadioOption<Plan>[] = [
  { description: 'For one person', label: 'Hobby', value: 'hobby' },
  { description: 'For a small business', label: 'Pro', value: 'pro' },
  { description: 'For a whole company', label: 'Team', value: 'team' },
];

export class PlanStep extends Jadis {
  static readonly selector = 'plan-step';

  templateHtml(): Node {
    // value="free" does not compile. Without <Plan>, the type is read from the options.
    return (
      <JlRadioGroup<Plan>
        label="Plan"
        options={PLANS}
        value="pro"
        variant="cards"
        onChange={(value) => choosePlan(value)}
      />
    );
  }
}

PlanStep.register();
```

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### With descriptions

```html
<jl-radio-group label="Plan" legend value="pro" options='[{"description":"One project, community support.","label":"Hobby","value":"hobby"},{"description":"Unlimited projects, email support.","label":"Pro","value":"pro"},{"description":"SSO, audit logs and a contract.","label":"Enterprise","value":"enterprise"}]'></jl-radio-group>
```

### Horizontal

A disabled option is skipped by the arrow keys.

```html
<jl-radio-group label="Size" legend orientation="horizontal" value="m" options='[{"label":"Small","value":"s"},{"label":"Medium","value":"m"},{"label":"Large","value":"l"},{"disabled":true,"label":"XL (sold out)","value":"xl"}]'></jl-radio-group>
```

### Cards

```html
<jl-radio-group
  label="Plan"
  variant="cards"
  orientation="horizontal"
  value="pro"
  options='[{"description":"One project, community support.","label":"Hobby","value":"hobby"},{"description":"Unlimited projects, email support.","label":"Pro","value":"pro"},{"description":"SSO, audit logs and a contract.","label":"Enterprise","value":"enterprise"}]'
></jl-radio-group>
```

### Cards, stacked

```html
<div class="narrow">
  <jl-radio-group label="Plan" variant="cards" value="hobby" options='[{"description":"One project, community support.","label":"Hobby","value":"hobby"},{"description":"Unlimited projects, email support.","label":"Pro","value":"pro"},{"description":"SSO, audit logs and a contract.","label":"Enterprise","value":"enterprise"}]'></jl-radio-group>
</div>
```

### Disabled

```html
<jl-radio-group label="Frequency" legend disabled value="weekly"
  options='[{"value":"daily","label":"Daily"},{"value":"weekly","label":"Weekly"}]'></jl-radio-group>
```

### Listening

The paragraph listens to change.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <jl-radio-group
    class="demo-theme"
    label="Theme"
    orientation="horizontal"
    value="system"
    options='[{"value":"light","label":"Light"},{"value":"dark","label":"Dark"},{"value":"system","label":"System"}]'
  ></jl-radio-group>
  <p class="muted demo-out">Theme: system.</p>
</div>
```

```js
const group = root.querySelector('.demo-theme');
const out = root.querySelector('.demo-out');
group.events.register('change', (value) => {
  out.textContent = `Theme: ${value}.`;
});
```
